goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the embed_category site setting lookup returns no row; execute(...)[0]['id'] raises on fresh installs where the setting is absent or matches no category name, and the same pattern repeats at line 18 for uncategorized_category_id

[BUG] The adapter hardcodes pathFor() to /admin/customize/embedding for every operation, so all embeddable-host CRUD hits the wrong routes: create gets 404, update PUTs to a controller that persists nothing, and destroyRecord 404s; the real resources :embeddable_hosts routes are unreachable from this UI

adjudication.rationale: The hardcoded `pathFor()` in `app/assets/javascripts/admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` applies only to the `embedding` model’s adapter, not to `embeddable-host` CRUD. The `embeddable-host` records created in the UI (`this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`, `host.save`, `host.destroyRecord`) will use the default `RestAdapter` logic. This diff explicitly adds `'embeddable-host'` to `ADMIN_MODELS` and updates `basePath()` to normalize underscores (`type.replace('_','-')`), which routes `embeddable-host` requests under `/admin/`, matching `resources :embeddable_hosts` in `config/routes.rb`. So the claim that embeddable-host CRUD hits `/admin/customize/embedding` and makes `/admin/embeddable_hosts` unreachable is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] SQL string interpolation of user-controlled embeddable_hosts setting values into INSERTs in the migration breaks on single quotes and is an injection vector

[ADVISORY] The plural hydration branch in store.js crashes on a null *_ids key (TypeError when serializer emits null ids for empty associations) and the || [] fallback is dead code, leaving undefined entries from failed _lookupSubType

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`if (m[2])`) unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`. If a payload contains `*_ids: null` (or any non-array), this will throw a `TypeError` at runtime. Also, `hydrated || []` is ineffective because `.map` always returns an array, and the code does not filter out falsy results from `_lookupSubType`, so the resulting association array can contain `undefined` entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'save changes' action is a no-op end to end: update({}) PUTs to embedding#update which never persists anything, and there is no save button in the template, leaving dead scaffolding

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin-embedding` controller action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, and a corresponding PUT route/controller action `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` that only re-renders the current OpenStruct embedding without persisting anything. The template `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` contains no button or binding that triggers `saveChanges`, so this path is effectively dead scaffolding. Actual persistence happens per-host via `embeddable-host` component calling `host.save(props)` against `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, so the no-op update path is not an end-user defect but is incomplete/unused code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] update and destroy with a nonexistent id in embeddable_hosts_controller raise NoMethodError on nil, producing a 500 instead of a 404 for stale/deleted records
[ADVISORY] create_table :embeddable_hosts with force: true silently drops a pre-existing table, causing unrecoverable data loss if the migration is re-run

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table of the same name before recreating it. If the migration is run in an environment where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., partially applied/failed migration, manual table creation, or a re-run outside the normal once-only migration flow), this would silently destroy existing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Migration dereferences execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category unconditionally; raises NoMethodError when embed_category was never set, breaking rake db:migrate on fresh installs

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` unconditionally. If that SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., fresh install where `embed_category` no longer exists—this diff removes `embed_category` from `config/site_settings.yml` and deletes it from `site_settings` at the end of the migration), then `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, breaking `db:migrate`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Data migration interpolates legacy embeddable_hosts value directly into INSERT INTO ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...) without quoting/escaping, causing SQL syntax errors or injection on hosts containing single quotes
[BUG] EmbeddableHostsController#update passes unguarded where(id:).first result to save_host, raising NoMethodError on nil and returning 500 instead of 404; same unguarded-first pattern in destroy

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that renders serializer without reading params; frontend saveChanges silently discards data and returns success while nothing is written — route, controller action, and JS action should be implemented or deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` which simply re-renders the serializer for an `OpenStruct` (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`) and never reads/writes params, so the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint is effectively a no-op. On the frontend, `admin-embedding` controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would report success while persisting nothing. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t expose any “save changes” UI and host changes are persisted through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save`, `destroyRecord`), so this is more an unused/incomplete endpoint/action than a user-visible correctness defect in the shown UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New controller specs only assert class inheritance; no tests exercise create, update, destroy, the category_id.blank? fallback, or render_json_error branch, leaving the nil-id crash and blank-category normalization regression-silent

adjudication.rationale: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` but do not handle the not-found case. If `params[:id]` is invalid/missing, `host` is nil and `save_host(host)` will raise a NoMethodError at `host.host = ...`, and `destroy` will similarly crash at `host.destroy`. This is a real, diff-introduced correctness issue; the new controller specs only asserting inheritance wouldn’t catch it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] EmbeddableHost validation regex requires a lettered TLD (\.[a-z]{2,5}), rejecting localhost, IP addresses, and long or hyphenated TLDs with a generic format error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added model `EmbeddableHost`, `validates_format_of :host` uses `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), which strictly requires a dot + alphabetic TLD of length 2–5. This will reject valid embeddable hosts such as `localhost`, IP literals (e.g. `127.0.0.1`), and modern longer TLDs (e.g. `.technology`), preventing admins from saving those hosts and thus preventing embedding for them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Store's plural hydration branch can include undefined members when ids aren't found in side-loaded payload since || [] only guards the whole-array case, and singular vs plural branches have divergent miss-behavior contracts

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` the new plural hydration branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => this._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` while always `delete obj[k]`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array, `|| []` never protects against missing lookups; if `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null` for an id not present in the side-loaded payload, the resulting relationship array will contain undefined entries. This is also divergent from the singular branch, which only sets/deletes when hydration succeeds, leaving the original `_id` otherwise. That inconsistency and potential undefined members are real, diff-introduced correctness issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Format-drift on port: the embeddable_host validation regex permits host:port and before_validation doesn't strip the port, but the lookup uses uri.host which never includes the port, so a ported host like localhost:3000 can never match and becomes a silently dead allowlist entry

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `validates_format_of :host` explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`). The `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not remove `:port`, so a saved record can be `example.com:3000`. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which never includes the port, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Missing schema invariants: no index on host causing a full-table scan on the lower(host) = ? hot path, no UNIQUE constraint on host allowing silent duplicates, and category_id has no FK to categories so deleting a category leaves dangling references surfacing as undefined in the client and nil category in TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embeddable_hosts` with `CreateEmbeddableHosts` but no indexes or constraints: the migration defines `t.string :host` and `t.integer :category_id` with no `add_index` and no UNIQUE constraint/FK. Meanwhile the hot-path lookup `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, which will indeed be a full-table scan without an appropriate (functional) index, and duplicates are possible without a uniqueness constraint. The FK/dangling-category part is plausible because there’s no referential integrity and client code/template expects `host.category` (`embeddable-host.js.es6` uses `host.category.id`, template uses `{{category-badge host.category}}`), but the claim about TopicEmbed.import yielding a nil category is not strictly shown (it passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, which could still be a stale integer).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Store.js plural-ids hydration branch maps _lookupSubType results with 'hydrated || []': null/undefined elements for missing ids remain in the array (the || [] never fires since an array with nulls is truthy), causing null.get('host') errors in consumers

Since `map` always returns an array, `hydrated || []` never replaces it, so missing lookups become `undefined`/`null` entries in the array. Additionally, the original `*_ids` field is deleted even if some/all lookups fail, so consumers can end up iterating `colors`/`embeddable_hosts` and calling methods on null elements (and they also lose the id list fallback).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-43 — no test for the no-match case when EmbeddableHost.record_for_host returns false; eh.try(:category_id) on false → nil, PostCreator receives category: nil, and regressions in this handling would not fail any spec

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:12-15 — test 'raises an error with a missing host' no longer tests deny-by-default semantics for the no-hosts-configured state; removed embeddable_hosts = nil precondition means a regression reintroducing permissive behavior when table is empty has no spec guard

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the deny condition is now `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (no longer tied to `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` being blank). The spec `it "raises an error with a missing host"` removed the explicit `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil`, but it also does not set any `referer`, so it will fail due to a missing/invalid referer regardless of whether the `embeddable_hosts` table is empty. That means the spec no longer specifically guards the "deny when no hosts are configured but a referer is present" behavior (empty DB state + valid referer), which is a distinct, newly-relevant condition after the migration to `EmbeddableHost`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — migration crashes with NoMethodError on any site that never set `embed_category`: the query returns zero rows, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises, aborting db:migrate on deploy; a renamed category also makes the join miss and crash

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when selecting the category for the old `embed_category` setting. If the query returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` was never set, or its stored value no longer matches any `categories.name` due to renaming), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration. The later `if category_id == 0` fallback won’t be reached because the exception occurs first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — dead guard `cmd_tuples > 0` on a SELECT means the backfill never runs (cmdtuples is 0 for SELECT in PostgreSQL), while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old site settings — embeddable-host lists permanently deleted with no replacement rows, causing InvalidAccess errors on embedded feeds

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the backfill from the old `site_settings` row is guarded by `if embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. `execute("SELECT ...")` returns a PG result where `cmd_tuples` for a SELECT is 0 in PostgreSQL, so this condition can prevent the migration from copying any existing `embeddable_hosts` values into the new `embeddable_hosts` table. Immediately after, it unconditionally runs `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`, which would drop the old settings even when no replacement rows were created. That would leave no allowed hosts, and since embed access control was switched to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., in EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?), embedding would start failing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — irreversible migration with no rollback: `change` migration with raw SQL inserts and DELETE FROM site_settings cannot restore deleted settings on rollback; a failed or re-run migration leaves old data destroyed with no path back

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` with multiple `execute` calls (raw INSERTs and `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`). Rails cannot automatically infer a reversible rollback for these operations, and there is no explicit `down` method to restore deleted SiteSetting rows. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about irreversibility/data preservation on rollback, but it does not break forward behavior in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — backfill interpolates host values raw into SQL, bypassing quoting and the model's normalization: old-format values like `http://discourse.org` are stored with the scheme so host matching never matches them, and a single quote in a value makes the INSERT raise

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the backfill does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, directly interpolating unquoted/unsanitized host strings into SQL. This can break on values containing `'` and is unsafe. It also bypasses `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` normalization (stripping `http(s)://` and paths), so old setting entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` would be persisted with scheme/path. Later matching uses `URI(url).host` and `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, which would not match those unnormalized records.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — `force: true` on `create_table` drops any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table on re-run, destroying admin-entered host/category data

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists at migration execution time, potentially wiping existing `embeddable_hosts` data. However, under normal Rails operation this migration runs only once (tracked in `schema_migrations`), so it’s not a guaranteed defect introduced by the diff—more of a risky/needless data-destruction behavior in atypical re-run/partial-migrate scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — embed category resolved by `site_settings.value = categories.name` join: if the category was renamed, the join misses and falls back to uncategorized, silently reclassifying embeds; fallback read `[0]['value']` crashes if the uncategorized setting is absent

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` derives `category_id` via `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. If `embed_category` stores a category name and that category has since been renamed, the join returns no rows, `category_id` becomes 0 and the code silently falls back to uncategorized, changing embed categorization. Additionally, the fallback `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value']` will raise if that query returns no rows (e.g., missing setting), since `[0]` would be `nil`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] — deploy-window break: settings deleted by the migration while old-code pods are still running and reading them — during rolling deploys old app instances read now-deleted settings and embed retrieval fails mid-rollout with no way to reconfigure via old UI

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` deletes the `site_settings` rows for `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). In the pre-change codepath (i.e., old pods during a rolling deploy), embed access checks and embed topic creation relied on `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` / `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` and `SiteSetting.embed_category`. With those settings removed mid-deploy, old instances would see them as blank and reject embeds (or mis-categorize), causing a deploy-window behavioral break exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:11-18 — `update` and `destroy` fetch `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no nil check; a stale/unknown id raises NoMethodError (`nil.host = ...` in `save_host`, `nil.destroy`), returning a 500 where a 404 belongs and a generic error to the client.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then used without checking for nil. If the id is stale/unknown, `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` on nil (NoMethodError), and `destroy` will call `host.destroy` on nil, producing a 500 instead of a proper 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:50-54 — the `delete` action chains `destroyRecord().then(...)` with no `.catch`; on failure the rejection is unhandled, `deleteHost` is never sent, the row silently stays in the table, and the admin gets no error feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` with no error handling. Unlike `save()`, which ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, a failed `destroyRecord()` promise will reject without being caught, providing no admin feedback and leaving the UI state unresolved (the row remains because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:11-14 — the `update` action never reads `params` or persists anything; the PUT endpoint returns 200 success for a silent no-op. It should 405/404 or not exist, since scripted embedding config gets a false success today.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (lines shown in diff) only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists any changes. The routes add `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, so the API will return a 200-style serialized response for a PUT that is effectively a no-op. While the current UI doesn’t appear to call `saveChanges` from the new `embedding.hbs` template (so it may be unused), the finding about misleading success semantics for the PUT endpoint is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7 — `this.get('embedding').update({})` has no rejection handler and no `isSaving` guard; it's a latent unhandled-rejection trap, and once `update` gains real persistence the save button becomes double-clickable with failures swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` without a `.catch(...)` (or other rejection handling) and without any `isSaving`/disabled-state guard in the controller. If `update` returns a promise and the request fails, that rejection would be unhandled. That said, the diff’s `embedding.hbs` template doesn’t show any save button/wiring to `saveChanges`, so the “double-clickable save button” aspect isn’t directly verifiable from this PR; it’s more of a forward-looking robustness concern than a current functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:9-13 — `record_for_host` returns `false` instead of `nil` on unparseable input; combined with `eh.try(:category_id)` in topic_embed.rb:36, a `false` return raises NoMethodError rather than falling back to nil — a trap for future callers treating it as 'record or nil'.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does return `false` on invalid/unparseable input (`return false unless uri.present?`, etc.). However, `topic_embed.rb` uses `eh.try(:category_id)`, and in Rails `try` is defined for `false`/`nil` and returns `nil` when the receiver doesn’t respond to the method. Therefore `false` here does *not* raise `NoMethodError`, and the specific claimed failure mode is not supported by the code shown.
